login_route_android_ech_title: Strict ECH preflight + reduced-security login bridge
login_route_bridge_title: Fixed Pixiv IP + reduced-security login bridge
login_route_compatible_title: Fixed Pixiv IP + full TLS verification
login_route_android_ech_body: Rust first verifies that the target accepts ECH. The official Android page then connects to a fixed Pixiv IP through a one-time local TLS bridge. The web bridge disables upstream SNI and certificate verification; token exchange after the callback returns to mandatory ECH with certificate verification.
login_route_bridge_body: The official Android page and the token exchange after its callback both connect to built-in Pixiv IP addresses with upstream SNI and certificate verification disabled. The bridge does not log request bodies, but an intermediary may read or alter passwords, verification codes, and tokens.
login_route_ech_body: Rust verifies that the target accepts ECH before opening the page. TLS for the official page itself is managed by the platform WebView; PixNya does not present platform state as a verifiable ECH Accepted result.
login_route_compatible_body: The login WebView still verifies SNI and certificates using the original hostname. Token exchange after the callback connects to a built-in Pixiv IP with SNI and certificate verification disabled, so an intermediary may read or alter tokens.
login_route_standard_body: The official page uses system DNS, proxy settings, and platform TLS. PixNya does not inject scripts or read page input.

login_risk_api_summary: Compatible mode includes a reduced-security API route
login_risk_bridge_ech: The WebView verifies a one-time local certificate for this session. The bridge then connects to a built-in Pixiv IP with upstream SNI and server certificate verification disabled. An attacker may read or alter sign-in traffic. The bridge does not parse or log request bodies, but decrypted data passes through app memory. Later token exchange returns to verified, mandatory Rust ECH.
login_risk_bridge_compatible: The WebView verifies a one-time local certificate for this session. The bridge then connects to a built-in Pixiv IP with upstream SNI and server certificate verification disabled. An attacker may read or alter sign-in traffic. The bridge does not parse or log request bodies, but decrypted data passes through app memory. Later token exchange also uses reduced-security direct access, so refresh and access tokens may be stolen.
login_risk_desktop_compatible: The login WebView retains end-to-end TLS. OAuth token exchange after the callback, API requests, and images use fixed IP addresses with SNI and certificate verification disabled. An attacker may steal refresh or access tokens or alter responses.
